question: The live animal trade has ground to a halt due to outbreaks in south-eastern Europe of peste des petits ruminants (PPR) and sheep and goat pox. According to data submitted by Romania to the AGRIFISH Council meeting of 29 September, the country has not exported a single head of sheep so far in 2026 – down from 1.

2 million between June and December 2023 – and culled over 235 000 animals between 2024 and 2026, resulting in an estimated economic fallout of more than EUR 150 million. However, these prolonged restrictions are also hurting farms whose livestock is healthy, and nothing has been done to help the farmers involved cope with the resulting revenue losses and higher feed bills. I therefore ask the Commission: 1.

How could it apply the regionalisation principle provided for in Regulation (EU) 2016/429 more flexibly so that healthy animals in unaffected areas can, subject to enhanced veterinary checks, be put on the market?

What mechanisms – including the agricultural reserve, the exceptional measures outlined in Article 220 of Regulation (EU) No 1308/2013 and the co-financing instruments supporting veterinary emergency measures – could it make use of to compensate the indirect losses mentioned above?

Could it share the timeline for the revision of the EU’s animal health legislation and for updating the EFSA assessment, including as regards animal vaccination and the movement of vaccinated livestock?
